correctness.rationale: Two independent endpoint-uniform chords on two unit circles with separation 2-delta are not motion-invariant line samples. Transforming uniform endpoints into unoriented line normal phi and signed arcsine offset gives exact crossing subdensity q_delta(z)=1_lens*pi^-4 integral |sin(phi-psi)| / [sqrt(1-(n_phi dot(z-c_-))^2)sqrt(1-(n_psi dot(z-c_+))^2)] dphi dpsi. The segment restriction is exactly membership in both disks, not merely supporting-line intersection. With z=(delta*x,sqrt(delta)*y), lens inequalities approach D={y^2+2|x|<1}, area(D)=4/3; the angular integral divided by log(1/delta) converges to 2*pi on the interior. The shown logarithmic boundary bounds make the convergence L1, and hence probability is (8/(3*pi^3))*delta^(3/2)*log(1/delta)(1+o(1)); conditional location converges in total variation to density 3/4 on D, with vertical density 3/4*(1-y^2) and moment 1/5. Inspected checker.py and independently checked that small-delta angular quadrature heads toward coefficient 2*pi; Monte Carlo at delta=.02 is not a proof of this limit.
